tspan.tspan: Figure 4. Analysis of the influence of trophic mode on principal component 1 (PC1). Trophic mode refers to the distinction between a
clade of ectomycorrhizal (EM) Amanita that are obligate symbionts, a clade of saprotrophic (SAP) Amanita, a clade of unknown trophic
mode consisting of A. inopinata and relatives. For context on the status of the unknown group see Supplemental Figure 1 and 2. (a)

text.tspan: Naive comparison of trophic mode and PC1. The difference between these three groups is non significant (p = 0.203). (b)
tree of Amanita overlaid with PC1
. When accounting directly for phylogenetic relatedness, there is no difference in PC1 between the

tspan.tspan: trophic mode groups (phyloANOVA: p = 0.731) in regards to PC1. Moreover, over the entire genus Amanita, there is no phylogenetic
signal and the PC1 trait appears to evolve unpredictably and not gradually (Blomberg’s K: 0.000002, Pagel’s λ: 0).
